					<div id="mw-content-text" class="mw-body-content"><div class="mw-subjectpageheader">
</div><div class="mw-content-ltr mw-parser-output" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-mw-parsoid-version="0.24.0.0-alpha18" data-mw-html-version="2.8.0"><section data-mw-section-id="0" id="mwAQ"><div class="shortdescription nomobile noexcerpt noprint searchaux" style="display:none" about="#mwt1" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwAg" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"Short description","href":"./Template:Short_description"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"Internet puzzle and mystery"}},"i":0}}]}">Internet puzzle and mystery</div><span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_short_description"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Short_description_is_different_from_Wikidata"></span>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt2" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwAw" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"For","href":"./Template:For"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"the taxon of insects"},"2":{"wt":"Cicada"}},"i":0}}]}"><style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1368532237" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" about="#mwt3" data-mw="{"name":"templatestyles","attrs":{"src":"Module:Hatnote/styles.css"},"body":{"extsrc":""}}">.mw-parser-output .hatnote{font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output div.hatnote{padding-left:1.6em;margin-bottom:0.5em}.mw-parser-output .hatnote i{font-style:normal}.mw-parser-output .hatnote+.mw-empty-elt+.hatnote{margin-top:-0.5em}@media print{body.ns-0 .mw-parser-output .hatnote{display:none!important}}</style></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt2" id="mwBA">For the taxon of insects, see <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cicada" title="Cicada">Cicada</a>.</div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBQ"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cicada_3301_logo.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBg"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cicada_3301_logo.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/7/7e/Cicada_3301_logo.jpg/250px-Cicada_3301_logo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" data-file-width="405" data-file-height="246" data-file-type="bitmap" height="152" width="250" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/7/7e/Cicada_3301_logo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled 2x" class="mw-file-element" id="mwBw"></a><figcaption id="mwCA">Cicada 3301 logo</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwCQ"><b id="mwCg">Cicada 3301</b> are three sets of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puzzle" title="Puzzle" id="mwCw">puzzles</a> posted under the name "3301" online between 2012 and 2014. The first puzzle started on January 4, 2012,<sup about="#mwt6" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-1"}}"><a href="#cite_note-1" id="mwDA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDg">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDw">]</span></span></a></sup> on <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4chan" title="4chan" id="mwEA">4chan</a>,<sup about="#mwt9" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-DT_2-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"DT"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-DT-2"}}"><a href="#cite_note-DT-2" id="mwEQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEw">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwFA">]</span></span></a></sup> and ran for nearly a month. A second round began on January 4, 2013, and a third round was posted on <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter" title="Twitter" class="mw-redirect" id="mwFQ">Twitter</a> on January 4, 2014.<sup about="#mwt12" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-3"}}"><a href="#cite_note-3" id="mwFg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwFw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGA">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt15" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-4"}}"><a href="#cite_note-4" id="mwGg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwGw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwHA">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwHQ">]</span></span></a></sup> The third puzzle remains unsolved. The stated intent was to recruit "intelligent individuals" by presenting a series of puzzles to be solved; no new puzzles were published on January 4, 2015. A new clue was posted on Twitter on January 5, 2016.<sup about="#mwt18" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-5"}}"><a href="#cite_note-5" id="mwHg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwHw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIA">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt21" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-6"}}"><a href="#cite_note-6" id="mwIg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwIw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJA">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Cicada 3301 posted their last verified <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenPGP" title="OpenPGP" id="mwJg">OpenPGP</a>-signed message in April 2017, denying the validity of any unsigned puzzle.<sup about="#mwt24" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-threat_stack_website_7-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"threat stack website"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-threat_stack_website-7"}}"><a href="#cite_note-threat_stack_website-7" id="mwJw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwKA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKQ">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwKw"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cicada3301's_First_Message.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwLA"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cicada3301's_First_Message.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Cicada3301%27s_First_Message.jpg/250px-Cicada3301%27s_First_Message.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" data-file-width="509" data-file-height="503" data-file-type="bitmap" height="247" width="250" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Cicada3301%27s_First_Message.jpg/500px-Cicada3301%27s_First_Message.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail 2x" class="mw-file-element" id="mwLQ"></a><figcaption id="mwLg">The first message of Cicada 3301 posted on <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4chan" title="4chan" id="mwLw">4chan</a>, beginning the first set of puzzles</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwMA">The puzzles focused heavily on <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_security" title="Data security" id="mwMQ">data security</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptography" title="Cryptography" id="mwMg">cryptography</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steganography" title="Steganography" id="mwMw">steganography</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet" title="Internet" id="mwNA">Internet</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anonymity" title="Anonymity" id="mwNQ">anonymity</a>.<sup about="#mwt27" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-mentalfloss_8-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"mentalfloss"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-mentalfloss-8"}}"><a href="#cite_note-mentalfloss-8" id="mwNg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwNw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwOA">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwOQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt30" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-WashingtonTimesErnst_9-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"WashingtonTimesErnst"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-WashingtonTimesErnst-9"}}"><a href="#cite_note-WashingtonTimesErnst-9" id="mwOg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwOw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwPA">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwPQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt33" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Telegraph2_10-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Telegraph2"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Telegraph2-10"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Telegraph2-10" id="mwPg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwPw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQA">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQQ">]</span></span></a></sup> It has been called "the most elaborate and mysterious puzzle of the Internet age",<sup about="#mwt36" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-metro_11-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"metro"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-metro-11"}}"><a href="#cite_note-metro-11" id="mwQg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwQw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwRA">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwRQ">]</span></span></a></sup> and is listed as one of the "top 5 eeriest, unsolved mysteries of the Internet" by <i id="mwRg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post" title="The Washington Post" id="mwRw">The Washington Post</a></i>,<sup about="#mwt39" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-12" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-12"}}"><a href="#cite_note-12" id="mwSA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwSQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwSg">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwSw">]</span></span></a></sup> and much speculation exists as to its function. Many have speculated that the puzzles are a recruitment tool for the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NSA" title="NSA" class="mw-redirect" id="mwTA">NSA</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIA" title="CIA" class="mw-redirect" id="mwTQ">CIA</a>,<sup about="#mwt42" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:2_13-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":2"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-:2-13"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:2-13" id="mwTg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwTw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwUA">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwUQ">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MI6" title="MI6" id="mwUg">MI6</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mossad" title="Mossad" id="mwUw">Mossad</a>, a "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masonic_conspiracy" title="Masonic conspiracy" class="mw-redirect" id="mwVA">Masonic conspiracy</a>",<sup about="#mwt45" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-14" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-14"}}"><a href="#cite_note-14" id="mwVQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwVg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwVw">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwWA">]</span></span></a></sup> or a cyber mercenary group.<sup about="#mwt46" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-DT_2-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"DT"}}"><a href="#cite_note-DT-2" id="mwWQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwWg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwWw">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwXA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt47" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-mentalfloss_8-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"mentalfloss"}}"><a href="#cite_note-mentalfloss-8" id="mwXQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwXg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwXw">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwYA">]</span></span></a></sup> Others have stated Cicada 3301 is an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternate_reality_game" title="Alternate reality game" id="mwYQ">alternate reality game</a>, although no company or individual has attempted to monetize it.<sup about="#mwt48" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-metro_11-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"metro"}}"><a href="#cite_note-metro-11" id="mwYg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwYw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwZA">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwZQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" id="mwZg" data-mw="{"autoGenerated":true}"></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwZw" aria-labelledby="Purpose"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Purpose">Purpose</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Cicada_3301&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Purpose"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwaA">The stated purpose of the puzzles each year was to recruit "highly intelligent individuals", although the ultimate purpose remains unknown.<sup about="#mwt49" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-DT_2-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"DT"}}"><a href="#cite_note-DT-2" id="mwaQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwag"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwaw">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbA">]</span></span></a></sup> Theories have included claims that Cicada 3301 is a secret society with the goal of improving <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptography" title="Cryptography" id="mwbQ">cryptography</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privacy" title="Privacy" id="mwbg">privacy</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anonymity" title="Anonymity" id="mwbw">anonymity</a> or that it is a cult or religion.<sup about="#mwt52" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-RS_15-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"RS"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-RS-15"}}"><a href="#cite_note-RS-15" id="mwcA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwcQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwcg">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwcw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt55" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-WNYC_16-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"WNYC"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-WNYC-16"}}"><a href="#cite_note-WNYC-16" id="mwdA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwdQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwdg">[</span>16<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwdw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt58" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-DaileyTim_17-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"DaileyTim"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-DaileyTim-17"}}"><a href="#cite_note-DaileyTim-17" id="mweA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mweQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mweg">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwew">]</span></span></a></sup> According to statements of several people who solved the 2012 puzzle, 3301 typically uses non-puzzle-based recruiting methods, but created the Cicada puzzles because they were looking for potential members with cryptography and computer security skills.<sup about="#mwt59" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-RS_15-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"RS"}}"><a href="#cite_note-RS-15" id="mwfA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwfQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwfg">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwfw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="2" id="mwgA" aria-labelledby="Resolution"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Resolution">Resolution</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Cicada_3301&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Resolution"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwgQ">The first puzzle of 2013 was solved by Marcus Wanner.<sup about="#mwt63" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Great_Big_Story_18-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Great Big Story"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Great_Big_Story-18"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Great_Big_Story-18" id="mwgg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwgw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwhA">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwhQ">]</span></span></a></sup> According to him, those who solved the puzzles were asked questions about their support of information freedom, online privacy and freedom, and rejection of censorship. Those who answered satisfactorily at this stage were invited to a private forum, where they were instructed to devise and complete a project intended to further the ideals of the group.<sup about="#mwt64" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-RS_15-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"RS"}}"><a href="#cite_note-RS-15" id="mwhg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwhw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwiA">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwiQ">]</span></span></a></sup> He did not finish his work on a method of general decryption, and the website was removed.<link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_with_unsourced_statements" about="#mwt60" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwig" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"citation needed","href":"./Template:Citation_needed"},"params":{"date":{"wt":"December 2021"}},"i":0}}]}"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_unsourced_statements_from_December_2021" about="#mwt60"><sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;" about="#mwt60" id="mwiw"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (December 2021)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup> A fellow winner documented her experience with the project on her YouTube account, "Nox Populi". Its description reads: "A series by one of the 2013 winners of the Cicada 3301 puzzle, showing the step by step solving process as well as discussing a more realistic, fact based view of the organization."<sup about="#mwt67" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-19" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-19"}}"><a href="#cite_note-19" id="mwjA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwjQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwjg">[</span>19<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwjw">]</span></span></a></sup> Currently, she facilitates community efforts surrounding Cicada 3301 on a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discord" title="Discord" id="mwkA">Discord</a> server. Other communities of solvers are still found on message boards and forums.<sup about="#mwt70" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-20" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-20"}}"><a href="#cite_note-20" id="mwkQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwkg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwkw">[</span>20<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwlA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<section data-mw-section-id="3" id="mwlQ" aria-labelledby="Types_of_clues"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Types_of_clues">Types of clues</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Cicada_3301&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Types of clues"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwlg"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cicada_3301_poster_locations.png" class="mw-file-description" id="mwlw"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cicada_3301_poster_locations.png" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/Cicada_3301_poster_locations.png/250px-Cicada_3301_poster_locations.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" data-file-width="3961" data-file-height="661" data-file-type="bitmap" height="42" width="250" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/Cicada_3301_poster_locations.png/500px-Cicada_3301_poster_locations.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail 2x" class="mw-file-element" id="mwmA"></a><figcaption id="mwmQ">Locations of the physical paper signs from the 2012 puzzle</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwmg">The Cicada 3301 puzzles used both online and physical clues, including digital images containing hidden information, a telephone message, websites, and paper signs bearing QR codes. Solvers encountered cryptographic and steganographic techniques, along with references to literature, poetry, art, and music.<sup about="#mwt71" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-DT_2-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"DT"}}"><a href="#cite_note-DT-2" id="mwmw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwnA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwnQ">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwng">]</span></span></a></sup> Each clue was signed by the same <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenPGP" title="OpenPGP" id="mwnw">OpenPGP</a> private key to confirm authenticity.<sup about="#mwt72" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Telegraph2_10-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Telegraph2"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Telegraph2-10" id="mwoA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwoQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwog">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwow">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt75" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-21" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-21"}}"><a href="#cite_note-21" id="mwpA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwpQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwpg">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwpw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="4" id="mwqA" aria-labelledby="Allegations_of_illegal_activity"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Allegations_of_illegal_activity">Allegations of illegal activity</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Cicada_3301&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Allegations of illegal activity"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwqQ">In 2012, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investigations_Police_of_Chile" title="Investigations Police of Chile" id="mwqg">Investigative Police (PDI)</a> in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Andes_Province,_Chile" title="Los Andes Province, Chile" id="mwqw">Los Andes Province</a> of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile" title="Chile" id="mwrA">Chile</a> claimed that Cicada 3301 is a "hacker group" and engaged in illegal activities. Cicada 3301 responded by issuing a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenPGP" title="OpenPGP" id="mwrQ">PGP</a>-signed statement denying any involvement in illegal activity.<sup about="#mwt78" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-andesonline_22-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"andesonline"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-andesonline-22"}}"><a href="#cite_note-andesonline-22" id="mwrg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwrw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwsA">[</span>22<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwsQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt81" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-pastebin_23-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"pastebin"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-pastebin-23"}}"><a href="#cite_note-pastebin-23" id="mwsg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwsw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwtA">[</span>23<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwtQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwtg">In July 2015, a group calling themselves "3301" hacked into <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planned_Parenthood" title="Planned Parenthood" id="mwtw">Planned Parenthood</a>'s database;<sup about="#mwt84" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-24" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-24"}}"><a href="#cite_note-24" id="mwuA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwuQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwug">[</span>24<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwuw">]</span></span></a></sup> however, the group appeared to have had no association with Cicada 3301.<sup about="#mwt87" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-25" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-25"}}"><a href="#cite_note-25" id="mwvA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwvQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwvg">[</span>25<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwvw">]</span></span></a></sup> Cicada 3301 issued a PGP-signed statement saying that they "are not associated with this group in any way, nor do [Cicada 3301] condone their use of our name, number, or symbolism".<sup about="#mwt90" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-26" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-26"}}"><a href="#cite_note-26" id="mwwA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwwQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwwg">[</span>26<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwww">]</span></span></a></sup> The hacker group later confirmed that they were not affiliated with Cicada 3301.<sup about="#mwt93" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-27" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-27"}}"><a href="#cite_note-27" id="mwxA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwxQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwxg">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwxw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="5" id="mwyA" aria-labelledby="Legacy_and_popular_culture"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Legacy_and_popular_culture">Legacy and popular culture</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Cicada_3301&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Legacy and popular culture"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwyQ">The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy" title="United States Navy" id="mwyg">United States Navy</a> released a cryptographic challenge based on the Cicada 3301 recruitment puzzles in 2014, calling it Project Architeuthis.<sup about="#mwt96" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-28" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-28"}}"><a href="#cite_note-28" id="mwyw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwzA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwzQ">[</span>28<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwzg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt99" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-29" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-29"}}"><a href="#cite_note-29" id="mwzw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw0A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw0Q">[</span>29<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw0g">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mw0w">The plot of "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautilus_(Person_of_Interest)" title="Nautilus (Person of Interest)" id="mw1A">Nautilus</a>", a 2014 episode of <i id="mw1Q"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Person_of_Interest_(TV_series)" title="Person of Interest (TV series)" id="mw1g">Person of Interest</a></i>, featured a large-scale game very similar to the Cicada 3301 puzzles. Both feature a series of worldwide cryptographic puzzles; as the title implies, these feature the image of a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautilus" title="Nautilus" id="mw1w">nautilus</a> shell instead of a cicada logo.<sup about="#mwt102" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-30" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-30"}}"><a href="#cite_note-30" id="mw2A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw2Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw2g">[</span>30<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw2w">]</span></span></a></sup> <i id="mw3A">Person of Interest</i> creator <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Nolan" title="Jonathan Nolan" id="mw3Q">Jonathan Nolan</a> and producer Greg Plageman said in an interview that Cicada 3301 was the inspiration for the episode: "I'm particularly fascinated by the subject underneath ["Nautilus"]. Look up Cicada 3301 on the Internet. It's a very interesting concept out there that we then put into a larger story that connects to our show".<sup about="#mwt105" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-31" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-31"}}"><a href="#cite_note-31" id="mw3g"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw3w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw4A">[</span>31<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw4Q">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mw4g">The organization is the subject of the 2021 comedy-thriller film <i id="mw4w"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_Web:_Cicada_3301" title="Dark Web: Cicada 3301" id="mw5A">Dark Web: Cicada 3301</a></i>.<sup about="#mwt108" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Phreaker_32-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Phreaker"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Phreaker-32"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Phreaker-32" id="mw5Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw5g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw5w">[</span>32<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw6A">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt111" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Cicada_33-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Cicada"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Cicada-33"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Cicada-33" id="mw6Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw6g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw6w">[</span>33<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw7A">]</span></span></a></sup> Directed by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Ritchson" title="Alan Ritchson" id="mw7Q">Alan Ritchson</a>, who co-wrote the script with Joshua Montcalm, it stars <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Kesy" title="Jack Kesy" id="mw7g">Jack Kesy</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conor_Leslie" title="Conor Leslie" id="mw7w">Conor Leslie</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Funches" title="Ron Funches" id="mw8A">Ron Funches</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Holden-Ried" title="Kris Holden-Ried" id="mw8Q">Kris Holden-Ried</a>, Andreas Apergis, and director Ritchson. The film follows a hacker who participates in Cicada's recruitment game while evading the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Agency" title="National Security Agency" id="mw8g">National Security Agency</a> (NSA).<sup about="#mwt114" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-RedBand_34-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"RedBand"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-RedBand-34"}}"><a href="#cite_note-RedBand-34" id="mw8w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw9A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw9Q">[</span>34<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw9g">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt117" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-DarkWeb_35-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"DarkWeb"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-DarkWeb-35"}}"><a href="#cite_note-DarkWeb-35" id="mw9w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw-A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw-Q">[</span>35<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw-g">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
